metaDescription: Taking on design and frontend development projects: from an idea to a working interface. Design systems, Jamstack and headless CMS. How to work with me and how to get in touch.

hero.description: Frontend developer & Designer. I design interfaces that I can implement myself. I program what I have designed.

rows.label: Approach
rows.value: Design systems, Jamstack and headless CMS

rows.label: Formats
rows.value: A consultation, a task, a project or work in your team

help.title: How I can help
help.description: Three areas. You can take them separately or together.

design.title: Design
design.text: I work out what the user needs and turn it into a clear interface: from scenarios and prototypes to finished screens and a design system.

development.title: Development
development.text: I code what I designed — or what another designer drew. A website, a landing page or a content project often doesn't need a separate backend: the interface is built on Next.js, and the content lives in a headless CMS like Sanity or Strapi, where it's edited without a developer. I build such projects end to end. If you already have a backend, I work with its API.
features: Backend-free projects on a headless CMS

ai.title: AI automation
ai.text: I've built AI features in a product and automation around it: text pre-moderation via OpenAI, Telegram bots, support request analysis. I can build AI into your product or use it to take routine work off your team.
features: AI in development: code, reviews, tests

why.title: Why one person for design and code
why.description: Time and meaning get lost between a mockup and the code. When one person does both, less gets lost.

usual.title: Usually
usual.text: Every clarification is another round between two people.

me.title: With me
steps: I build it in code right away
me.text: A decision is made once and checked in the browser right away.

items.title: Decisions based on data
items.text: I rely on interviews, usability tests and product metrics, not on taste.

items.title: A quick start
items.text: I start a new project on my own design system: buttons, inputs and the dark theme are already done.

items.title: Products and studios
items.text: I've worked both at product companies and at studios: I know how work runs both in a product and with clients.

items.title: Leadership experience
items.text: I led a frontend team of 5: priorities, reviews, releases and stack decisions.

items.title: Tidy code
items.text: I set up linting, git hooks, tests and CI/CD so the project is safe to keep developing.

items.title: Remote work
items.text: I live in Sochi and work remotely. We'll agree on communication and call times up front.

projects.title: My projects
projects.description: Open-source libraries I build myself — from Figma mockups to publishing on npm.

designSystem.title: Design system
designSystem.text: Styles and React components with matching Figma files. This site is built on it.

steps.title: You describe the task
steps.text: What the product is, what needs to be done and by when. If the task is still vague, we'll work it out together.

steps.title: We agree on a format
steps.text: A consultation, a small task, a whole project or work in your team. Before starting, I give you the scope and timeline.

steps.title: I work and show progress
steps.text: In small steps and with a working version, not just a description. We take feedback into account as we go.

steps.title: I hand over the result
steps.text: The code goes to your repository, the mockups to your Figma, plus documentation.

fit.title: Who I'm a fit for
yes: you need one person for both design and frontend
the product needs an interface with tables, charts and complex scenarios
you need to build an MVP or a new section of a service quickly
you need a website or a content project without a separate backend
you need to bring order to the interface: tokens, components, a design system
you want to add AI to the product or get rid of routine
no: most of the work is backend
you need branding, illustrations or video
you need someone in the office full-time

contact.title: Have a task in mind?
contact.text: Get in touch about working together. Describe the task in a couple of sentences — I'll reply with how I can help and how best to organize the work.
